steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Darius sent a fleet in 490 BC to punish Athens and Eretria for supporting the Ionian Revolt; Eretria was sacked

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Persian force landed at Marathon, guided by the exiled Athenian tyrant Hippias

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Athenians marched to Marathon and were joined by 1,000 Plataeans; they were heavily outnumbered

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Miltiades persuaded the Athenians to attack; the Greeks strengthened their wings and thinned their centre

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Why did Darius invade Greece in 490 BC? | Q: How did Miltiades win the Battle of Marathon? | Q: Why was the decision to attack controversial?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: To punish Athens and Eretria for supporting the Ionian Revolt and to extend Persian control into mainland Greece. Darius also wanted to restore Hippias as a puppet tyrant in Athens. | Miltiades strengthened both wings of the Greek line while thinning the centre. steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Marathon = 490 BC, Darius punishing Athens/Eretria Miltiades' tactic: strong wings, thin centre, double envelopment Sparta delayed by the Carneia festival (religious prohibition) Marathon became a powerful Athenian myth of democratic courage
